notes:
The Uptown Tenderloin Historic District nomination (08001407, listed 5 February 2009), read for the theatre addresses named in issue #302 and for nothing else. Its section 7 inventory runs to roughly four hundred properties across thirty-three blocks and is unread; that pass is a batch of its own and is filed as issue #304, not attempted here.

One of the fifteen theatre parcels in #302 falls inside the district: 76-80 Turk Street, which the inventory records as the Gaiety Theater. The other fourteen are outside the boundary, and the nomination's own Theaters section says why the district holds so few — the post-fire theatres rebuilt on Market Street and in the adjacent Market Street Theater and Loft district, and only a handful ever stood inside these thirty-three blocks.

The reference number is the trap in this batch. The Uptown Tenderloin is 08001407; 08000209, which is what a plausible guess at an early-2008 San Francisco listing produces, serves a nomination for Johnston's Inn in Paris, Kentucky, with San Francisco nowhere in it. The NPS index is the only way to a reference number.

coverage.remaining: The section 7 inventory of 08001407 — roughly 400 properties over 33 blocks — is unread apart from the Turk Street page carrying #302's address. Three further theatre buildings were seen in passing while searching it and are recorded in issue #304, which is that pass: 814-820 Larkin Street (Larkin Theater 1920-1962, moving picture theater 1919, architect William Knowles), 35-65 Mason Street (Ferris Harriman Theater and Hotel 1911, theatre converted to a garage in 1929) and the Hotel Cecil at 156 Eddy Street (Moderne blade sign lettered Exit Theater). Also still unread in this source: 1990-1999 (17 listings), the rest of 2000-2009 (21), 2010-2015 (15), 2016-2023 (15), and the five district nominations of 1982-1989.
coverage.note: A targeted read, not a pass: one inventory row out of roughly four hundred. Counting it as 1 examined nomination and 1 mention would overstate what was read of the document and understate what is left, so the remaining note carries the real shape.

findings.description: Built as the Gaiety Theater, a conversion of stores and a loft to a theatre, to the design of the architect Earl B. Bertz. Two storeys, reinforced concrete with a stucco facade and cast ornament, pilasters and pointed arches at the second level, Gothic ornamentation on a two-part commercial block composition, with a horizontal blade sign.

resolution.method: EAS puts 76 and 80 TURK ST on parcel 0340011 and on no other, and the page is at the lower number. The inventory's own block/lot column prints '540/11', which is an OCR misread of 340/11: the first row on the same page reads '340/7' correctly for 34-48 Turk Street, and the five consecutive rows 34-48, 50, 62-64, 66-74 and 76-80 carry lots 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11, which are exactly the assessor's lots for the published pages at those numbers (0340007, 0340008, 0340010, 0340011). Block 0540 is in the Western Addition and holds no Turk Street frontage.

findings.description: The decorative griffins and the parapet were removed, and the storefronts remodelled.

publish.note: No date the page's one date-ordered timeline can place it on. 'After 1990s' is the nomination's whole statement, and the site's rule is that dates are ranges with a stated end, not arithmetic left to the reader. The fact is kept here rather than published as an entry with no year.
